crossStoryFindings: Current-source semantics are split across the epic: process materials, checkpointing, and rebuild planning use `resolveActiveProcessSourceAttachments`, but refresh targeting, project-shell refresh eligibility, and informed-work provenance still trust raw durable `currentMaterialRefs.sourceAttachmentIds`.
Soft detach and process-scope shadowing therefore stop at the read-model boundary; some runtime paths still treat detached or shadowed rows as current after the UI has hidden or replaced them.
The provenance API shape is ahead of the runtime: degraded visibility modes such as `redacted` exist in the contract and renderer, but not in any real production write path.
architectureFindings: The tech design makes active-source resolution the canonical rule for combining project-scoped and process-scoped sources, but `RuntimeSourceHydrationExecutor` and `DefaultSourceProvenanceService.recordInformedWorkForCurrentSources` bypass that policy and reconstruct their own source sets from raw refs.
Soft detach is implemented durably (`detachedAt`, `detachedByUserId`) and respected by the main readers, but older raw-ref consumers can still pull detached rows back into refresh/recovery decisions.

The published provenance contract advertises `currentAttachmentVisibility: redacted`, but the implementation has no architecture path that detects revoked enrichment access and materializes that state.
epicCoverageAssessment: Epic gate passed: `corepack pnpm run verify-all` completed successfully on May 4, 2026. The `test:e2e` leg is still scaffold-only and prints `SKIP: test:e2e scaffolded in Story 0; no executable suite yet`.
Automated coverage exercises attach/update/detach flows, branch-drift freshness, refresh settled/pending/failed responses, and ready/degraded provenance rendering.

Coverage does not exercise shadowed-source refresh/recovery or informed-work provenance recording when both project- and process-scoped ids remain durably current; the only explicit shadowing check I found is contract/fixture-level (`tests/service/server/source-management-contracts.test.ts:41-62`), and the redacted provenance path is only test-seeded (`tests/service/server/source-management-api.test.ts:1099-1167`).
productionPathFindings: Source refresh is wired to real GitHub/provider seams, but its working-set planner still rehydrates from raw durable source ids, so detached or shadowed rows can flow back into a real provider hydration.
The `redacted` provenance visibility branch is currently contract-only: no production writer emits `access_revoked` or any other degraded provenance row for that path.

Process execution still uses the shared Epic 3 placeholder script payload, so the provenance hooks run against a non-domain-specific execution path even though persistence and checkpoint integrations are real.

blockingFindings.title: Refresh planning bypasses active-source resolution and can rehydrate detached or shadowed-out sources
blockingFindings.evidence: `RuntimeSourceHydrationExecutor.refreshRecoverableSource()` resolves target ownership and builds the hydration plan from raw `currentMaterialRefs.sourceAttachmentIds` (`apps/platform/server/services/sources/source-refresh.service.ts:92-159,215-240`) instead of the active-source resolver used by checkpointing and rebuild planning (`apps/platform/server/services/processes/active-process-sources.ts:13-62`, `apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/process-environment.service.ts:751-760,1269-1289`). Because process-scoped attach only appends the new id and detach only stamps `detachedAt` (`convex/sourceAttachments.ts:148-158,279-317`), refreshing one source can still target or hydrate rows that the canonical current-source model has already shadowed or detached. The same raw ids also drive `projectRefreshTargetCount` in the project shell (`apps/platform/server/services/projects/readers/source-section.reader.ts:36-66`).

blockingFindings.title: Informed-work provenance ignores shadowing and can record duplicate or wrong-scope source relationships
blockingFindings.evidence: `recordInformedWorkForCurrentSources()` iterates `currentMaterialRefs.sourceAttachmentIds` directly and records every distinct id (`apps/platform/server/services/sources/source-provenance.service.ts:36-75`). When a process-scoped attachment shadows a project-scoped sibling, both ids remain durably current because process attach only appends the new id (`convex/sourceAttachments.ts:148-158`), while the canonical current-source read model collapses them via `resolveActiveProcessSourceAttachments()` (`apps/platform/server/services/processes/active-process-sources.ts:13-62`). `buildSourceProvenanceEntry()` then exposes whichever recorded row was stored, including its scope/access/hydration (`apps/platform/server/services/sources/source-provenance.service.ts:174-230`), so provenance can claim both attachments informed the run or attribute informed work to the shadowed project-scoped row that the process materials view no longer shows.

blockingFindings.title: The shipped runtime cannot produce the required redacted provenance state
blockingFindings.evidence: The response contract and renderer support `currentAttachmentVisibility: 'redacted'` / `degradationReason: 'access_revoked'` (`apps/platform/shared/contracts/source-management.ts:97-152`, `apps/platform/server/services/sources/source-provenance.service.ts:202-228`), but the only production write path always persists provenance as `entryStatus: 'ready'` with `degradationReason: null` (`apps/platform/server/services/sources/source-provenance.service.ts:153-171`). The only exercised redacted path is test-seeded data (`tests/service/server/source-management-api.test.ts:1099-1167`). No non-test code writes `access_revoked` or any other degraded provenance row.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Source provenance is wired to the shared placeholder execution payload
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: Process execution still defaults to `buildDefaultScriptPayload()` and its embedded placeholder script (`apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/script-execution.service.ts:9-104`). The epic's real provenance hooks run off that execution/checkpoint path (`apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/process-environment.service.ts:549-568,830-839`), so informed-work and code-update provenance are currently attached to placeholder execution behavior until process-type-specific orchestration lands.

The fix shape for provenance `access_revoked` is still unsettled: the codebase needs either a real write-time producer or a read-time derivation rule for redacted entries.

crossStoryFindings: Process-scoped shadowing is only enforced in read/checkpoint paths; provenance recording and runtime refresh still consume raw current source refs, so the same process can show one canonical source in materials while recording or hydrating a different set underneath.

The source-management stack treats project source listings as exhaustive, but the underlying Convex query truncates them to 200 rows. Older attached/current sources can silently disappear from provenance and hydration flows even though their durable rows still exist.
architectureFindings: Tech Design Q6/Q7 says process-scoped rows shadow project-scoped rows for process current-source behavior, but `DefaultSourceProvenanceService` and `RuntimeSourceHydrationExecutor` bypass `resolveActiveProcessSourceAttachments` and therefore drift from the declared resolver contract.

The durable/read contract for attached sources is not pagination-safe: `convex/sourceAttachments.ts` caps project source listings at 200, while refresh/provenance builders assume that list is the full authoritative set.

productionPathFindings: Runtime refresh is wired to real provider adapters, but the shadowed-source path can hydrate the wrong working set because `RuntimeSourceHydrationExecutor` rebuilds refresh plans from raw material refs instead of the canonical active-source resolver.

Informed-work provenance still depends on the default Epic 3 execution placeholder payload, so part of this epic's production provenance path still runs through a non-domain-specific execution script.
Redacted provenance is representable in contracts/tests, but runtime code does not currently produce `access_revoked` provenance entries; existing coverage seeds that degraded state directly.

blockingFindings.title: Shadowed project-scoped sources are still recorded as canonical process provenance
blockingFindings.evidence: `DefaultSourceProvenanceService.recordInformedWorkForCurrentSources` iterates raw `currentMaterialRefs.sourceAttachmentIds` (`apps/platform/server/services/sources/source-provenance.service.ts:36-74`). Process-scoped attaches append their id without removing the shared project id (`convex/sourceAttachments.ts:442-457`), while shadowing is only defined in `apps/platform/server/services/processes/active-process-sources.ts:13-63`. Reproduced with an in-memory store: one project-scoped plus one process-scoped `acme/repo@main` produced 2 `informed_work` provenance rows instead of the single visible process-scoped source.

blockingFindings.title: Refresh can target a shadowed project source and hydrate the wrong working set
blockingFindings.evidence: `RuntimeSourceHydrationExecutor.resolveTargetProcessId` and `refreshRecoverableSource` use raw `currentMaterialRefs.sourceAttachmentIds` and then feed them straight into `planHydrationWorkingSet` (`apps/platform/server/services/sources/source-refresh.service.ts:92-159,223-320`). That bypasses the active-source resolver that the main environment hydration path uses (`apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/process-environment.service.ts:1275-1289`). Reproduced with an in-memory store: refreshing a project-scoped source shadowed by a process-scoped sibling settled successfully and the adapter received both source ids in the hydration plan.

blockingFindings.title: Project source listings are hard-capped at 200 rows, breaking older current-source/runtime paths
blockingFindings.evidence: `convex/sourceAttachments.ts:42-53` returns project source summaries with `.take(200)`. `DefaultSourceProvenanceService` and `RuntimeSourceHydrationExecutor.buildAdapterHydrationPlan` both treat `listProjectSourceAttachments` as exhaustive (`apps/platform/server/services/sources/source-provenance.service.ts:41-54,87-95`; `apps/platform/server/services/sources/source-refresh.service.ts:260-318`). Reproduced by simulating the real capped store behavior: when a process current ref pointed at the 205th attachment, provenance recording created 0 rows; the refresh path would hit `HydrationPlan references sourceAttachmentId ... not in the project's source listing.`

nonBlockingFindings.title: Informed-work provenance still runs through the default execution placeholder
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: `ScriptExecutionService` still defaults every execution to `buildDefaultScriptPayload`, whose source is explicitly labeled `liminal-build default execution placeholder` and writes the `shared Epic 3 placeholder execution payload` (`apps/platform/server/services/processes/environment/script-execution.service.ts:9-24,76-104`). That does not break Epic 6 storage directly, but the production provenance signal for `informed_work` is still tied to a placeholder execution lane.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Redacted provenance is test-seeded rather than runtime-produced
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: `createProvenanceRecord` always persists `entryStatus: 'ready'` with `degradationReason: null` (`apps/platform/server/services/sources/source-provenance.service.ts:153-171`), and no runtime path writes `access_revoked`. `buildSourceProvenanceEntry` can emit `currentAttachmentVisibility: 'redacted'` only when a stored degraded record already carries that reason (`apps/platform/server/services/sources/source-provenance.service.ts:174-230`).
